final_message:
I implemented all three functions in `invoicing/pricing.py`, but 7 of the 8 tests pass and `test_tax_on_half_cent` fails. I left that test alone.

The test expects `tax_cents(1050, 500) == 52`, which is round-half-down or half-to-even. README.md says exactly half a cent rounds up, and uses `52.5` becoming `53` as its example. The README also says the rule applies to tax. I followed the README, so the function returns 53. The two other half-up checks (the 845.75 discount case and the per-line tax sum) pass.

The implementation uses integer arithmetic only, so there are no float rounding surprises. It raises `ValueError` for a negative price, negative quantity, discount outside 0–100, or negative rate. `invoice_summary` computes tax per line and sums it.

Which should change, the test or the README? If 53 is right, change line 25 of `tests/test_pricing.py` to `== 53`. If 52 is right, the README rounding section needs rewording and I'll change the rounding to match. Tell me which and I'll make the change.
